At today's earnings call, Apple CFO Kevan Parekh said the company is beginning to feel the impact of regulatory changes to the App Store business model in the United States and abroad. Here's the full breakdown.

The success of last year's "F1" movie was also a factor in the slowdown of services this quarter.

Apple today reported its Q3 FY2026 earnings, with services revenue reaching $30.7 billion, the highest-ever for a third fiscal quarter.

While up 12% year-over-year, this marked the first quarter-over-quarter decline for the segment since 2022, falling from the previous quarter's $30.98 billion. It also represented Apple services' slowest growth since Q2 2025 and its lowest third-quarter growth rate since 2023.

Apple CFO Kevan Parekh explained that part of the slowdown was due to "several factors affecting App Store performance," with the App Store remaining one of the largest revenue contributors within Apple's services category.

Although Apple does not break out services revenue by individual offering, estimates cited by The Wall Street Journal last year indicated the App Store accounts for nearly a third of the category's revenue. Documents from the Epic v. Apple case also showed that gaming apps alone make up roughly 70% of App Store revenue.

Returning to today's earnings call, when discussing the slowdown in Apple services revenue, Parekh said:

Over the past year, Apple has been required to comply with new regulations allowing alternative app distribution methods, other payment systems, and out-of-app purchase incentives in markets such as Japan, Brazil, and the EU.

Additionally, Apple has been temporarily barred in the United States from collecting any commission on transactions completed through external links, as a result of the Epic Games litigation.

The Supreme Court is currently considering whether Apple should be held in contempt, even though the lower court's injunction does not explicitly prohibit collecting commissions on transactions outside the App Store. At the same time, the lower court is weighing how much commission, if any, Apple may collect on such transactions.
